author: Frosty
text:
Hi everyone, Continuing down the path now with PAZs From the markepedia: PAZ P: The PAZ article is about getting an idea of where price is going to go so you will be able to pick a trade direction with a higher probability of success.

W: By practicing and doing your PAZ homework you will be able to identify the direction of price with a much higher success rate. Once you are able to identify the direction you can then focus on the best My current understanding of PAZs: - Essentially, from my understanding,PAZ is simply the space between FLs.

- To use this for our trading, we should just remember that when price enters a new PAZ from one side, price would then want to continue to go to the other side of the new PAZ. - To enter a new PAZ, price need to engulf the previous PAZ's FL. In RTM, we are taught that after price engulfs into a new PAZ without hitting the other side of the new PAZ, we can enter on the retrace to the FL that caused the engulf (many call this the DP/Decision Point, which, from what I understand, is also a FL).

- Since PAZs are defined as the space between FLs, then naturally there would be PAZ between PCP MPL and base of CP MPL, between two ends of a pole (LQ gap or wide range bars), and between the top and bottom of flags. The best trades should be taken at the edges of these PAZs, i.e.not inside a PAZ. - With the above logic, then we should be able to classify the regions on the chart as either a FL or a PAZ. - PAZs, like price movement, are fractal in nature as well. What looks like a single PAZ in one timeframe can have many FLs and smaller PAZs inside of it. The choice on how we should define our PAZs is ours to make according to which timeframe/scale we want to trade. - This part is if I didn't misunderstood bro Staurum and bro Enkim: Something that I learned from bro Staurum is that we should always look at the higher scale picture for any possible sign of FO that could happen to the lower scale price movement. Here is the post that hinted on this issue. The clue is to look at the HTF picture. Always make sure that the price movement in the HTF has already cleared the MPL of that HTF FL before trying to trade LTF FLs because if the HTF MPL hasn't been hit, price could fake past all of the LTF FLs and go for the HTF MPL, even if there was a valid engulf to the next PAZ edge. Bro Enkim wrote a note (here) that I understood only a few days ago. Thank you bro Staurum and bro Enkim - If price directly hits the other edge of a PAZ, then all trades are off until there is another engulf into another PAZ or if there is a LTF PA telling us to stay within the PAZ (this case, I believe is what we call flagging).

Apologies for the lack of charts, but I think the concept of "spaces between FLs" should be a clear picture if FLs has been properly understood.

As always, I appreciate any comments, hints, and corrections on this matter. Thank you everyone

Remember that I assumed that there are no HTF SR kinks in between. Happy to hear your or anyone's thoughts on this matter, if it is not too much to ask As for your question regarding the targets, to be honest I'm still confused as well about the answer to that question I have always tried to make it simple by finding the closest-to-price QM level in the FL on the same scale I am trading on, but this depends on whether there is a higher TF PA or not.

For example, if I am to trade short from the HTF UFL MPL and there was no HTF LFL engulf like in the drawing, I would be most inclined to target the closest QM level in the mouth of FL A for my runner position. The first target, which I would close 75% of my positions at, would be a QM level in the FL that breaks the LTF UFL in question (like what you said).

If there was a higher TF engulf, similar to the drawing, then my first target would be the closest QM level in the mouth of FL A, then the runner would be left for the QM level in the mouth of HTF LFL B.

author: Frosty
text:
Hi again everyone, As usual, hectic work schedule on my part so I can post less at the moment.

But I've also been studying in between work breaks and during my spare time, while balancing with the time spent with my wife and kid.

I still find this balancing life schedule hard, but I personally think it is necessary.

In the end, if I think about trading long and hard enough, I want to do it for the sake of giving my family the best I can.

This is mostly for the time spent with them and not so much about materialistic things. I believe trading as a career, if done properly, can achieve this kind of freedom.

With the usual self-help ramble done, hopefully, with these few posts, I can finally move on to the other processes other than technical aspect of trading, i.e. money management and, most importantly, psychology.

I will start with the Engulf and Fakeout.

From the markepedia: Engulf: P: "There is no Price Action without an Engulf" and it is what defines our trading. It is our leading "indicator" regarding price intentions. W: Forget about candle engulfs/engulfing patterns. What we look for is Flag Limit Engulfs. Through homework and experience you will learn which FL engulfs are real PA. Once a FL is engulfed price will want to go to the next, but we always have to be mindful of how much it can retrace.

My current understanding of Engulfs: - Real engulfs or PAs are defined as the consumption of all orders inside FLs, i.e. Engulfs arenot simply breaks of local SR, highs and lows, FTRs which are not FLs, or random supply demand zones. I always try to keep this one simple:If I can't find the FL that I think a price movement engulfs, just find the next clear FLs to see the engulf from and scratch the previous mentioned engulf interpretation.

- I always try to remember to draw FLs properly first before assessing engulfs from them. The markepedia gave us a hint on this:Through homework and experience you will learn which FL engulfs are real PA. What looks like a PA/engulf, could be a reaction off the real FL or true supply/demand which is obscured inside a large candle in the tick chart. Please see the following example for a real chart example: - The only useful engulf is the one that hasn't reached its target. We should only look for these types of engulfs. Engulfs that has reached its target is non-tradeable - About this part in the markepedia:Once a FL is engulfed price will want to go to the next, but we always have to be mindful of how much it can retrace, through screen time, I concluded that this has to do with the HTF FL that we want to trade from. The important question to ask about an engulf is:Did the engulf came from the last clean sets of orders, i.e. from the MPL? I would be very careful of trying to trade from a FL if previous price movement didn't clear the HTF FL MPL first beforehand, since a DM of the HTF price action could form after an engulf of a LTF FL if the ITs decide to clear all the orders in the HTF FL. This was my first question in thispostand the answer to that question is summed up in the previous sentences. In short:Always be mindful of the HTF picture, particularly their MPLs - A personal recipe of master Salivan's engulf, which can be read from the FOF Articlestates that the ITs can show their intention by engulfing LTF FL, while at the same time, not engulfing the HTF FL. Personally, for a noob trader such as myself, I believe it is best to leave this advanced master class concept for when we understand all other RTM puzzle pieces. I have not proven this concept myself, but I believe it is safer to wait for whole FL engulfs because there might be clean orders inside an even lower chart than the 1 minute chart, e.g. 10-second or tick charts, above or below the given 1-minute FL.

- An important article from master Salivan is theEngulf/Retrace Article. The conclusion that, I think, we should understand from this article is that: an engulf which didn't reach its' target, would surely have left a set or more clean orders from the FL it came from. It is the retrace to this price level with clean orders (FOF) that we should trade from.

- Also from the engulf/retrace article, the depth of retrace after an engulf depends on whether the target is an important FL or not (i.e. FTR).

Important FLs, from my studies, would have FOs in the form of QM levels that hasn't been touched. Master Mertch's charts show what these FOs look like. If the target is a FL with QM levels that are still clean, then a deeper retrace should be expected as these are ITs' price targets and they would want to get their last orders from the other side of the market to be closed in the FL with clean orders mentioned previously.

- Master Staurum created a helpful, three partposton FLs, Engulfs, and Targets with Master Salivan's answer in his journal that is very beneficial for everyone here.

- Also important from Master Harry:If you want to find good bouncy places you have to follow the order flow and see where it failed, where there are people (or robots) trapped.

- To sum up the wordy, mind-dumping words above:The useful engulf is the one that hasn't reached its target, which signals us to trade in the direction of the engulf from the source FL of the engulf, i.e. from places where people/robots are trapped, while keeping in mind the HTF picture for possible DM/FO scenario As usual, this is what I have learned and not necessarily the truth. The charts, and not my or anyone's words, would provide the ultimate truth.

Also, I would extremely appreciate any corrections in any of my flaws of thinking in any of the above points as I am still studying.

Hopefully nothing is way off the mark Thank you all in advance!

Next up would be the Fakeout and how to distinguish FO from engulf.

author: Frosty
text:
Next up is the FO and what distinguishes them from engulfs Markepedia doesn't have an entry on this, but I believe it is important to understand them and differentiate them from engulfs.

My current understanding of Fakeouts, Origins/Targets, Ignored Levels, QM, and DM: - To distinguish between FO and engulf, we should look to the FL they are reacting to. While an engulf consumes the FL they are reacting to, an FO stays within the confines of the FL. Please see this modified diagram from IF for my understanding of FOs: - A great explanation from Master Mertch's journal can be seenhere - FO's purpose is to create liquidity. They serve as targets and origins for ITs. These are the "tricks being played" part of the price action puzzle.

- A DM should be expected if FO level doesn't quite touch the MPL of the FL price is reacting to. A DM is essentially, Imho, a FO of a FO level.

- Targets and origins naturally has a double role. They both are one of the same thing. A long origin/source's target is a short origin/source and a short origin/source's target is a long origin/source. These are essentially LS kink / QM levels inside FLs.

- We should check LTF for each QM levels inside the FL we are interested in if we are entering our positions as they may be spiked on the way away from the FL. Do not trade the second and subsequent touches to a QM level if we do not have engulf away from the particular QM level. 1st time back has the most chance of a bounce.

- Quote:"Look for tricks being played on approach into places where tricks were played". My understanding of this quote:"Look for tricks being played on approach (BSZ, CP, CPLQ) into places where tricks were played (QM levels or LS kinks inside FLs). All should be done with proper PA/engulf in the right direction.

- As for Ignored levels, after many hours of studies, I would stick to just iQM levels that was inside a FL, like in my homework above. My current understanding is that the FO level should be inside the FL to validate the iQM, if the QM level doesn't get respected on the way back. iQM levels that wasn't created inside a FL, I would personally pass. iQM levels would create the next swap FL. Ignored CPs and SRs are left out at the moment.

I want to master a few things first at a time.

- For QM and DM understanding, at this point in my education, I understand it all comes down to finding pockets of trapped traders and robots, i.e. clean sets of orders. These can be seen through a LS level that hasn't been touched on the way away and, preferably, create some sort of BSZ or CP on the way to the true supply or demand. If we were to zoom in on LTF, at the tip of a DM, we would likely see a miniature QM formation.

DM and QM is a byproduct of the IT manipulation, imho. If MPL was taken by the QM's HH/LL, then QM level or LS kink will work. If MPL didn't get taken by the QM's HH/LL, then expect a DM to form.

- My understanding on the details of DM:here - My understanding on the details of QM:here - Ultimately, in the simplest form, as master IF said in one of his videos, we are trading from where the retail stop losses are From all of these technical summaries, I would combine all of these knowledge together to move on to "reading a session" exercises.

As always, I appreciate very much any corrections and guidance
